chose: Drop account.issuer column + index entirely (migration 1789578812345) and key accounts by providerId again
over: Only relaxing NOT NULL and leaving the column/index in place
because: better-auth 1.7.3 reverted issuer scoping; the 1.6/1.7.3+ account schema has no issuer, so the column is dead weight whose NOT NULL and compound unique index can only break inserts later. The stored value was one synthetic constant (local:atproto) so nothing is lost; down() restores it. Pinning back to 1.7.1 keeps a schema upstream has abandoned.

chose: grocery/randomizer/recipes-write db suites fail on main too, and the failure count moves between runs (3, 4, 5)
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
pre-existing shared-state flake between db suites (fileParallelism false, one shared dev DB, scratch rows leaking across files)
my local dev database has drifted from the migration chain (e.g. recipe_pending_image.source_url nullability) so the assertions test the DB, not the code
discriminatedBy: drop and re-migrate the local DB from empty (docker compose down -v; db:migrate:up), then run the three files twice: still failing from clean = real flake/bug; green = local drift

chose: local dev database drift — the assertions were testing my laptop's schema, not the code
because: Created an empty buttery_fresh database, ran db:migrate:up on it, and ran the same pnpm test:db against it: 343 passed / 343, 13 files, zero failures. The same command against the long-lived local buttery database fails 6.

chose: Load services/web/.env in vitest.config.ts so test:db is a bare 'vitest run --project db'
because: services/pipeline/vitest.config.ts already solves this exact problem this exact way, and matching it means one pattern per repo instead of two. railway run injected a dead dev-proxy DATABASE_URL (port 33628), so every db suite skipped or errored and the script had been silently useless. Node's loadEnvFile does not overwrite an already-set DATABASE_URL, so an explicit one still wins.
